plan.summary: Twelve-month, standard-mode plan on M&T Bank Corporation (MTB, NYSE), USD, as of 2026-09-25, answering three operator questions: commercial real estate exposure and its reserve coverage; whether net interest margin is at a cyclical peak given deposit repricing; and whether return on tangible common equity supports the market's multiple of tangible book. Evidence comes from FY2023-FY2025 10-Ks, the Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs, eight quarters of earnings releases and supplemental average-balance tables (Q3 2024 through Q2 2026), Q4 2025-Q2 2026 earnings call transcripts used only as dated management assertion, FFIEC Y-9C and call reports, Federal Reserve stress-test and capital-buffer disclosures, the 2026 proxy, and named market and rate sources for valuation inputs. Revised after review: transcripts added; the supplemental-table window extended to match the eight-quarter deposit-beta calculation; cost-of-equity provenance and a stated derivation rule for sustainable ROTCE; every source marked required or optional with its degradation path. This plan states no figure; all numbers are computed by code from fetched facts. Prior research is context only, never a source.

challenges.statement: The plan gathers earnings releases and supplemental tables but no earnings call transcripts or prepared management commentary. challenges.statement: The earnings_quality focus asks for realised deposit beta 'across the last eight quarters', but the planned earnings supplements cover only four quarters (Q3 2025 through Q2 2026). The section as scoped asks for a figure no planned source can establish at the stated granularity.
challenges.suggestion: Either extend the planned supplemental-table retrieval back to Q3 2024, or narrow the focus to the quarters actually sourced and state the shorter window explicitly in the section output.

challenges.statement: The valuation section's output — implied price-to-tangible-book from a residual-income model — is driven as much by cost of equity and 'sustainable ROTCE' as by anything in the filings, yet no source is named for the cost-of-equity inputs (risk-free rate is covered by H.15, but beta and equity risk premium are not) and no method is stated for deriving a sustainable ROTCE from the historical series. sections.focus: Core of operator question one and the funding leg of question two. From the FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q, establish loan composition: commercial real estate by property class (office, multifamily, retail, industrial), geography, fixed versus floating, and maturity/repricing schedule where disclosed. Pair with allowance for credit losses by portfolio segment, roll-forward, charge-offs, nonaccrual and criticised/classified balances, and coverage ratios. Then funding: deposit mix by type, non-interest-bearing share, estimated uninsured deposits, brokered and time deposits, short-term borrowings, long-term debt, and AFS/HTM securities with unrealised marks. Every item is a retrieval target; none is asserted here.

Operator question two. Decompose net interest income into earning-asset yields, interest-bearing liability costs, realised deposit beta and reported margin across the eight quarters Q3 2024 to Q2 2026, sourced from quarterly supplemental average-balance tables; if any quarter's supplement is unavailable, the section must state the shorter window actually computed rather than infer it from annual 10-K averages. Separate margin attributable to non-recurring items (purchase accounting accretion, recoveries, day-count, securities repositioning) from repricing. Retrieve Item 7A rate-sensitivity tables and any disclosed hedge notional and maturity ladder. Test fee-income mix and provision volatility.

Build the multi-year record later sections compute against: net interest income and margin, provision, non-interest income and expense, efficiency ratio, net income, average earning assets, average common and tangible common equity, goodwill and intangibles, and return on tangible common equity, from the FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 10-Ks plus 2026 interim filings. Include the People's United acquisition period so intangibles deducted from tangible equity are traceable to filings rather than inferred. This series is the input to the sustainable-ROTCE derivation used in valuation.

Operator question three, executed as an equity-side residual-income (excess return on tangible common equity) model with a dividend-discount cross-check, not an enterprise free-cash-flow DCF; the section must say so. Sustainable ROTCE is derived by a stated rule: the FY2023-FY2025 annual ROTCE series from historical_financial_analysis, adjusted by code to remove items earnings_quality flags as non-recurring, with the adjustment disclosed. Cost of equity by CAPM from a named risk-free source, a named beta vintage and a named published equity risk premium. Report implied price-to-tangible-book across a cost-of-equity range, never at a single point, against the observed multiple.

Rank by effect on the twelve-month view and tie each to a specific disclosure: CRE concentration and office/multifamily refinancing at maturity; reserve adequacy against criticised-loan migration; deposit competition and wholesale funding substitution; hedge roll-off and securities reinvestment spreads; unrealised securities losses against tangible equity; capital requirement and stress-buffer outcomes; operational, cyber and credit-rating risk. Cite the filing item that names each. Where filings give no quantified disclosure, mark the risk unverified rather than sizing it.

Three states for the twelve-month horizon with driver ranges code flexes: deposit beta and mix shift on margin; CRE loss content and provision build; earning-asset reinvestment spread under rising, flat and falling short-rate paths; buyback pace under alternative capital buffers; and cost of equity across its stated range. Each scenario outputs ROTCE and implied tangible-book multiple from the same engine. The 'has margin peaked' question is answered as a sensitivity result with a labelled judgement, not asserted.

State the thesis as falsifiable propositions keyed to the three operator questions, each with the evidence that would confirm or break it and the section holding that evidence. Distinguish what filings establish from forward judgements about margin trajectory and credit migration, and from management assertions taken from call transcripts, which are dated statements of intent or expectation and not established fact.

Break results by reportable segment as disclosed in the FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q - commercial bank, retail bank, institutional services and wealth management, and 'all other' - covering segment net interest income, provision, revenue and average loans and deposits. Purpose is to locate where CRE risk and deposit-cost pressure actually sit rather than treating the bank as one pool.

Trace deployment from cash flow statements, capital-action 8-Ks and the 2026 proxy: dividend declarations, repurchase authorisation and execution, CET1 and tangible common equity ratios, and the stress capital buffer constraining them. Establish whether earnings are being returned or held against credit and unrealised-loss uncertainty, since this governs the payout input to the residual-income and dividend-discount valuation.

Date-stamped events inside the horizon: the Q3 2026 earnings release and 10-Q (after the as-of date), Q4 and FY2026 results, the 2027 Federal Reserve stress-test cycle and resulting buffer, dividend and repurchase decisions, and disclosed CRE maturity concentrations. For each, state the observable that would move the thesis and the direction the evidence would point.

Compare this run's findings against the open questions the prior approved view left - whether CRE loss content has migrated, whether deposit repricing has continued, whether the equity premium to tangible book has changed. Every comparison must rest on evidence fetched in this run. Do not restate, cite or carry forward prior figures, ratings, betas, cost-of-equity estimates or valuation ranges; the platform rejects such citations in code.

warnings: Enterprise value and free cash flow to the firm are not meaningful for a bank: deposits and debt are raw material, not financing.

Capital adequacy, net interest margin and provisioning govern the valuation. The residual-income model offered here values the excess return earned on book value, and equals a dividend discount only under clean surplus: a bond book carrying unrealised losses through other comprehensive income is treated as fully earning.

themes.label: Commercial real estate credit cycle
themes.rationale: M&T carries a large CRE loan book relative to peers, including office and multifamily exposure inherited from People's United; credit quality and reserve builds are highly sensitive to CRE valuation and refinancing stress.

themes.label: Net interest margin sensitivity to rate cycle
themes.rationale: As a traditional spread lender, M&T's earnings are directly driven by Fed policy path, deposit repricing lags, and asset yield resets, making NIM trajectory a core determinant of its profitability.

themes.label: Regional bank deposit funding competition
themes.rationale: M&T competes for core deposits against larger banks and money-market alternatives; deposit cost inflation and mix shift toward higher-cost funding pressure its cost of funds and margin.

findings.statement: M&T Bank Corporation reports three reportable segments, consistently confirmed across 2023, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 filings.

Per the September 2026 investor presentation, M&T's H1 2026 results showed diluted EPS of $9.44 (+25% YoY) and net income of $1,482MM (+14% YoY), with return on tangible assets of 1.46% and return on tangible common equity of 16.5%.
Quarterly net income available to common stockholders was $781MM in Q2 2026 and $620MM in Q1 2026, following full-year 2025 net income available to common of $2,699MM.

M&T's 2026 outlook (as disclosed September 2026) guides taxable-equivalent net interest income of $7.2–$7.35 billion, fee income of $2.8–$2.85 billion, GAAP expense of $5.5–$5.6 billion, net charge-offs of ~37bps, and a CET1 ratio target of 10.0%–10.5%.

The company's loan portfolio is diversified across C&I, CRE, residential real estate, and consumer categories, with average loans excluding CRE growing 6% in both 2024 and 2025, and CRE balances inflecting upward (+5% QoQ EOP) in Q2 2026 after a multi-year decline.

Asset quality has materially improved: nonaccrual loans fell from $2,166MM (1.62% of loans) in 2023 to $1,208MM (0.84%) by Q2 2026, and criticized commercial loans fell from $12,579MM (14.0% of commercial loans) in 2023 to $5,852MM (6.5%) by Q2 2026 — company describes nonaccrual ratio as lowest since 2007.

caveats: Residual income equals the dividend-discount value only under clean surplus — that every gain and loss passes through profit, so book value moves only by earnings less dividends. A bank's available-for-sale securities move through other comprehensive income instead, so a book value carrying unrealised losses is treated here as fully earning.
No value is placed on anything beyond the explicit forecast: the excess return is assumed competed away at the end of it.

The two terminal treatments are opposite claims about competition, not two estimates of one number. Fading to nothing says a bank's excess return is competed away at the end of the forecast; perpetual growth says it never is. Both are shown because choosing between them is a judgement about banking, and presenting either alone would present that judgement as arithmetic.
The valuation assumes the bank earns above its cost of equity in perpetuity. Competition has historically removed such a spread.
